title: Treatment programs the City pays: in the federal locator, and in Medicaid
question: Is each organization the City pays for mental-health or drug and alcohol treatment listed in the federal treatment locator, and does Medicaid show treatment services under its name?
finding: 55 nonprofits were paid $801.5 million by the Department of Public Health since fiscal 2019 under contracts titled for mental-health or substance-use services. 12 are in both the federal locator and Medicaid treatment billing, 24 in Medicaid only, 2 in the locator only and 17 in neither ($58.1 million from the City; the largest is Central City Hospitality House, $21.5 million). Most of the Medicaid money for their treatment services is billed by someone else: $507.6 million under the City's provider numbers and $455.6 million under other bodies' numbers (83% of it other counties and public bodies), against $8.6 million under their own, 2018 to 2024.
how: City side: payments in the City's nonprofit spending file, Department of Public Health, fiscal 2019 to 2026, under contract titles that carry the ledger's words or abbreviations for mental-health and substance-use work (for example “DPH SUD Treatment Svcs”, “Methadone Services”, “DPH MH and SUD”), for organizations paid $100,000 or more; payees were matched to the project's nonprofit profiles by name. Federal locator: the 2,204 California listings on FindTreatment.gov (54 in San Francisco), matched by name; a match that is not word for word is labelled, and an organization counts as in the locator when a listing under its name is in San Francisco or one of the five neighbouring counties (listings elsewhere in California, often another program of a statewide body, have their own column). Names are matched on their words, allowing the same opening words where the ledger has cut a name short. Medicaid: money on mental-health and drug or alcohol codes (codes beginning H, and psychotherapy codes 90785 to 90899) billed by provider numbers registered under the organization's name, and money on the same codes where the organization is named as giving the service and another body, usually the City, billed. An organization counts as in Medicaid at $10,000.
limits: Being absent from the federal locator is not a fault: listing is voluntary, the locator shows only current listings, and a program can appear under a parent, a sister organization or the name of a site. Being absent from Medicaid treatment billing is not a fault either: the contract titles on file also cover prevention, peer advocacy, recovery housing, program evaluation and administration, which Medicaid may not pay for; some clients may not be eligible for Medicaid; and a program can bill through a number registered under a different name, or one outside the project’s provider universe. Contract titles are a rough guide to what was bought, and the City amount is everything paid under those titles, not only treatment. Organizations are matched by name, so a trade name can be missed. The Medicaid file withholds small cells and 2024 is preliminary. The row to read is the one in neither, and the question it raises is only what the contract paid for.
